hint: Watch for “the” versus “a” in the English.

corpus.en: A wolf does not follow the eagle.
The wolf does not follow elves.
A wolf does not follow the eagles.
Elves do not follow the wolves.
The eagles do not guard the towers.

accepted: the eagles do not follow a wolf
the eagles did not follow a wolf
the eagles are not following a wolf
toEnglish.explanation: S O V order. tuke-ko-mu = eagle-PL-DEF; manto-bo = wolf-ACC; re = NEG; agi-ne = follow-3PL.

toLang.prompt: The elves do not guard a tower.
toLang.explanation: S O V order. tetu-ko-mu = elf-PL-DEF; tentanta-bo = tower-ACC; re = NEG; binte-ne = guard-3PL.

grammar: Word order: subject, object, verb. With one participant: subject, verb.
Definite (“the”). A noun without it means “a” (or plain plural).
On the verb when the subject is plural.
Negation: a separate word before the verb.
explain.notes: Checked against 739 alternative analyses; the sentences rule out 728, including: -ko appears when: definite; -ko appears when: plural & definite.
